craft_notes: Sthāyin: the chief bath — the rite's summit. Sanskrit-first: viśeṣas tu (distinction-but) kept; ānanda-dravya kept bliss-substance (dravya kept as substance); śivamayīkṛtya kept gerund having-made-Śiva; tenaiva (by-that-very-one) kept the reflexive turn; tarpaṇam kept satisfying. Rows: 9 (worship→satisfaction→chief-bath triple verdict), 1 (‘chief bath’ closes — mukhya-snāna named last), 6 (iti verdict-voice). Close: 'thus the chief bath.' Rejected: ‘bliss-essence’ — killed: dravya is substance (thing, not quality); ‘by it’ — killed: tenaiva is by-that-very-one (the worship itself acts). Read aloud: BUT the-BLISS-sub-STANCE, a-BID-ing AS the-HER-o's-SUP-port, BY-look-ing, HAV-ing-MADE-it ŚI-va — RIGHT-there, THE-man-tra-CIR-CLE's-WOR-ship; THENCE BY-that-VER-y-ONE, BODY-and-BREATH-de-i-ty-CIR-CLE SAT-is-fied: THUS-the-CHIEF-bath.

lines: But the bliss-substance, abiding as the hero's support,
by looking, having made it Śiva — right there,
the mantra-circle's worship; thence by that very one,
body-and-breath deity-circle satisfied: thus the chief bath.
l4.sanskrit_cite: viśeṣas tu ānandadravyaṃ vīrādhāragataṃ nirīkṣaṇena śivamayīkṛtya tatraiva mantracakrapūjanam tataḥ tenaiva dehaprāṇobhayāśritadevatācakratarpaṇam iti mukhyaṃ snānam

reads_against.argmap: What is the chief bath? → The mukhya-snāna: ānanda-dravya seen in vīra-ādhāra and made Śiva, mantra-cakra pūjā, then tarpaṇa of the deity-circle abiding in body and breath.
c1_essence: The chief bath: bliss-substance hero-abiding made-Śiva, mantra-circle worshipped, deity-circle of body-and-breath satisfied by that very one.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vidhi weight (quiescence carrying ritual order)
